long_biography.plain_text:
Carroll grew up in Greensboro in a working-class family and began earning money through odd jobs while still a teenager. At fourteen, he bought and renovated a small house in Virginia with savings from mowing lawns, returning bottles and selling candy. After his father lost a grocery-industry job, they took on a custom-home project and performed much of the work themselves.

The father and son formalized their construction company in 1983, with Roy handling accounts and office work while his father led building crews. Carroll later bought the elder man's share and shifted from individual homes toward subdivisions and recurring rental income. Apartments became the portfolio's centre, followed by self-storage, industrial development, hotels and mixed-use projects.
